Sentinel Temperature Test (Tap Temperature Readings) - Monthly Visit

You are carrying out monthly sentinel temperature testing on the domestic hot and cold water systems.

The purpose of this task is to check that water temperatures are within safe limits to prevent the growth of Legionella bacteria.

- Test the first and last outlets on each hot and cold water line.
- Cold water should reach below 20C within 2 minutes.
- Hot water should reach 50C or above within 1 minute (55?C for healthcare sites).
- Record the temperature and the time taken to reach it.
- If temperatures are outside limits, recheck, report to the supervisor, and raise a note in JobLogic.
- Wipe probes between each test and ensure readings are taken accurately.

Your aim is to confirm the system is performing correctly and identify any outlets or systems where temperatures suggest potential stagnation or risk of Legionella growth.

Emergency Lighting - Monthly Visit

You are carrying out the monthly functional flick test on the building's emergency lighting system to confirm all fittings operate correctly when the mains power is interrupted.

Procedure:
- Isolate the lighting circuit using the local key switch or test point for each area.
- Confirm that all emergency lights illuminate immediately when power is cut.
Inspect fittings for:
- Damaged or failed lamps/LEDs
- Cracked or missing diffusers
- Incorrect or missing labelling
After checks, restore mains power and confirm charging indicators (usually green LEDs) are lit.

Record all results in the JobLogic form, noting any defects or non-functional fittings for follow-up repair.

1. Indoor Unit(s)

AHU Filters - Annual Visit

1. Safety Procedures
  1.1. Isolate electrical supply and apply lockout/tagout before opening access doors or servicing components.
  1.2. Check PPE and safe access arrangements.
  1.3. Review previous maintenance records.

2. Air Filtration & Airflow
  2.1. Inspect pre-filters and fine filters; measure differential pressure to determine if replacement is required.
  2.2. Check filter gaskets and frame integrity to ensure proper sealing.
  2.3. Listen for abnormal noise or vibration from fans and motors.
  2.4. Inspect fans and motors, including motor alignment, belt tension, and pulley condition.
  2.5. Lubricate bearings as required.
  2.6. Carry out motor insulation resistance testing.

3. Coils & Heat Recovery Systems
  3.1. Inspect thermal wheel/heat exchanger for correct rotation, belt tension, and seal condition.
  3.2. Check condensate drain pan and pipework; clean and ensure free drainage.
  3.3. Inspect heating and cooling coils for debris; clean using low-pressure water or approved chemical cleaner.
  3.4. Inspect all pipework connections (chilled water, heating, cooling) for leaks.

4. Electrical & Controls
  4.1. Measure and record motor voltage (V) and current (A).
  4.2. Tighten all electrical terminals.
  4.3. Inspect control panel and verify safety interlocks are functioning correctly.

5. Mechanical & Casing
  5.1. Check door hinges, latches, and seals; lubricate where necessary.
  5.2. Inspect and lubricate damper linkages, set screws, and blade operation.
  5.3. Inspect casing for corrosion; clean and treat with approved anti-corrosion coating where required.

6. Direct Expansion (DX) System (If Applicable)
  6.1. Check refrigerant circuit for leaks.
  6.2. Inspect refrigerant levels and compressor oil levels.

7. General Cleanliness
  7.1. Clean the AHU compartment, removing all dust and debris.

Installation of Sound-Dampening Panels

This quote covers the professional installation of sound-dampening panels in the designated location, as per the details below.

The below price includes the labour for secure installation, assuming the panels and necessary fixings are supplied by the client and the wall is suitable, as per the site specification (unless otherwise agreed).

Work Phases
1- Site Assessment & Preparation
Our team will assess the designated wall or ceiling area, planning the exact layout and ensuring the surface is clean and ready for installation. We will verify the suitability of the structure to securely hold the weight of the panels. Protective coverings will be laid down as needed.

2- Panel Installation
The sound-dampening panels will be carefully installed according to the agreed-upon pattern and alignment. They will be securely fixed using the appropriate adhesives and/or mechanical fixings (as specified), ensuring full surface contact for optimal sound absorption.

3- Finishing & Inspection
We will ensure all edges are neat and the installation is completed to a high aesthetic standard. The installation will be inspected to confirm secure placement and correct alignment.

4- Final Clean Up & Handover
All installation debris and packaging will be removed from the site, and the work area will be thoroughly cleaned.

Important Notes Regarding Additional Costs
Client-Supplied Items: This quotation is for installation labor only. The sound-dampening panels and all necessary fixings/adhesives must be supplied by the client.

Wall Suitability: This quote assumes the wall/ceiling is a standard, sound surface suitable for direct application. If the surface is uneven, weak, or requires strengthening, lining, or significant preparation, these additional works will be assessed and quoted separately.

Specialised Patterns: This quote assumes a standard installation pattern. If the installation requires complex cuts, highly intricate patterns, or work around numerous obstacles (e.g., numerous outlets, complex architectural features), additional labour costs may apply.

Incorrect Parts: If the client-supplied panels or fixings are incorrect, missing, or unsuitable for the wall type, we will be unable to complete the installation, and a new quotation will be required to cover a return to site at a later date.

FCU 4 Pipe - Half Yearly Visit

1. Safety and Initial Inspection
  1.1. Switch off the FCU and isolate the circuit breaker.
  1.2. Verify electrical isolation (lockout/tagout).
  1.3. Visually inspect the unit for external damage, vibration, or abnormal noise.
  1.4. Check duct insulation for damage or signs of mould.

2. Cleaning and Filter Maintenance
  2.1. Remove and clean or replace air filters (typically on a 30–90 day cycle).
  2.2. Clean the evaporator coil using an approved cleaner or vacuum.
  2.3. Clean the blower wheel, fan housing, and motor.
  2.4. Clean the drain pan and clear any blockages in the drain line.
  2.5. Clean the external casing.

3. Electrical and Mechanical Inspection
  3.1. Check electrical connections for tightness at the control panel.
  3.2. Inspect motor wiring for wear or damage.
  3.3. Measure and record motor amperage and voltage.
  3.4. Inspect fan motor operation for noise or vibration.
  3.5. Lubricate fan bearings and motors (if applicable).
  3.6. Check pulleys and belts for correct tension and signs of wear.

4. Plumbing and Controls
  4.1. Inspect valve actuators and pipework for leaks.
  4.2. Test motorised valves for correct operation.
  4.3. Check the function of the room thermostat.
  4.4. Inspect P-trap condition.

5. Final Testing and Reporting
  5.1. Restore power and switch on the unit.
  5.2. Verify smooth operation without vibration.
  5.3. Record supply air temperature.
  5.4. Complete a service report detailing findings, works carried out, and recommendations.

FCU VRF - Half Yearly Visit

1. Visual Inspection
  1.1. Check the general condition of the indoor unit and mounting.
  1.2. Inspect casing for damage, corrosion, and loose panels.
  1.3. Check air inlet and outlet for obstructions.

2. Filters
  2.1. Remove and clean air filters.
  2.2. Check condition of filters and replace if required.

3. Electrical Components
  3.1. Inspect electrical wiring and terminals; tighten connections.
  3.2. Check operation of PCB, sensors, and thermistors.
  3.3. Verify voltage and current draw.

4. Refrigerant Circuit
  4.1. Check refrigerant pipe insulation for damage.
  4.2. Perform leak test on indoor connections.

5. Fan & Blower
  5.1. Inspect fan and blower wheel for dirt or damage.
  5.2. Clean blower if required.
  5.3. Listen for unusual noise during operation.

6. Coils
  6.1. Inspect evaporator coil for dirt or damage.
  6.2. Clean coil using appropriate chemicals if required.

7. Drainage
  7.1. Check and clean drain pan.
  7.2. Flush drain line to ensure free flow.

8. Condensate Pump
  8.1. Isolate power before inspection.
  8.2. Inspect pump for cracks or damage.
  8.3. Remove and clean the pump tank, float switch, and check valve; ensure all parts move freely.
  8.4. Test operation by lifting the float switch to simulate water level.
  8.5. Verify discharge line is clear and correctly sloped.

9. Control & Communication
  9.1. Verify remote controller operation.
  9.2. Check indoor-to-outdoor communication signals.

10. Operational Test
  10.1. Measure supply and return air temperature differential.
  10.2. Check airflow rate.
  10.3. Confirm correct system response in cooling and heating modes.

VRF Outdoor Condenser Unit - Half Yearly Visit

1. Visual Inspection
   1.1. Check general condition of the outdoor unit.
   1.2. Inspect casing for corrosion, damage, and loose panels.
   1.3. Check for refrigerant oil stains or leaks.
   1.4. Ensure the surrounding area is free of debris and obstructions.

2. Electrical Components
   2.1. Tighten all electrical connections.
   2.2. Inspect contactors, relays, fuses, and wiring.
   2.3. Verify PCB and sensor operation.
   2.4. Measure and record voltage, current, and phase balance.

3. Refrigerant Circuit
   3.1. Check suction, discharge, and liquid line pressures.
   3.2. Record superheat and subcooling values.
   3.3. Check compressors for abnormal vibration or noise.
   3.4. Perform a refrigerant leak check.

4. Fans & Motors
   4.1. Inspect and clean fan blades.
   4.2. Check fan motor bearings.
   4.3. Verify fan speed and direction.
   4.4. Listen for unusual noise or imbalance.

5. Heat Exchangers (Coils)
   5.1. Inspect and clean condenser coils.
   5.2. Check coil fins for damage and straighten as required.
   5.3. Inspect coils for corrosion.

6. Drainage
   6.1. Clean drain pans and drain lines.
   6.2. Verify proper drainage flow.

7. Control & Communication
   7.1. Verify outdoor-to-indoor communication signals.
   7.2. Check system operation via controller/BMS.
   7.3. Update software/firmware if required.

8. Operational Test
   8.1. Run the system in cooling and heating modes.
   8.2. Record temperatures, pressures, and power consumption.
   8.3. Confirm correct system cycling.

Installation of Sound-Dampening Panels

This quote covers the professional installation of sound-dampening panels in the designated location, as per the details below.

The below price includes the labour for secure installation, assuming the panels and necessary fixings are supplied by the client and the wall is suitable, as per the site specification (unless otherwise agreed).

Work Phases
1- Site Assessment & Preparation
Our team will assess the designated wall or ceiling area, planning the exact layout and ensuring the surface is clean and ready for installation. We will verify the suitability of the structure to securely hold the weight of the panels. Protective coverings will be laid down as needed.

2- Panel Installation
The sound-dampening panels will be carefully installed according to the agreed-upon pattern and alignment. They will be securely fixed using the appropriate adhesives and/or mechanical fixings (as specified), ensuring full surface contact for optimal sound absorption.

3- Finishing & Inspection
We will ensure all edges are neat and the installation is completed to a high aesthetic standard. The installation will be inspected to confirm secure placement and correct alignment.

4- Final Clean Up & Handover
All installation debris and packaging will be removed from the site, and the work area will be thoroughly cleaned.

Important Notes Regarding Additional Costs
Client-Supplied Items: This quotation is for installation labor only. The sound-dampening panels and all necessary fixings/adhesives must be supplied by the client.

Wall Suitability: This quote assumes the wall/ceiling is a standard, sound surface suitable for direct application. If the surface is uneven, weak, or requires strengthening, lining, or significant preparation, these additional works will be assessed and quoted separately.

Specialised Patterns: This quote assumes a standard installation pattern. If the installation requires complex cuts, highly intricate patterns, or work around numerous obstacles (e.g., numerous outlets, complex architectural features), additional labour costs may apply.

Incorrect Parts: If the client-supplied panels or fixings are incorrect, missing, or unsuitable for the wall type, we will be unable to complete the installation, and a new quotation will be required to cover a return to site at a later date.

SCOPE OF WORKS

Project/Site: Neko Health Victoria System: VRF (Variable Refrigerant Flow) Air Conditioning System – condenser (roof) serving floors ground  Works Required: Repair/replacement of defective compression joints and full leak check of pipework, followed by return of system to service Reason for Works: Following the pressure and leak test carried out 14–16 August 2026, three confirmed leaks (and one possible further leak) were identified at compression joints on the original installation pipework leaving the condenser on the roof. Every accessible joint tested was found to be compromised. The system remains switched off with no cooling available at site. 

BACKGROUND

1.1 The system is served by a condenser on the roof, with pipework running down through the building 6 to the ground to serve the ground. It was originally installed as part of the Oktra fit-out.

1.2 The pressure and leak test carried out 14–16 August 2026 confirmed three leaks (Leaks 1–3) at compression joints on the pipework immediately outside the condenser, and indicated a possible fourth leak at the point the pipework enters the wall leading down to the 6th floor. Testing could not be completed beyond this point as the run could not be traced or accessed.

1.3 Neko Health's demise at this site covers the ground floor only. Floors 1–6 fall outside the demise and are not accessible to Up-fm unless separately arranged with the landlord/managing agent.

SCOPE OF WORKS

2.1 Attend site and liaise with site contact/building management on arrival and departure.

2.2 Isolate the system electrically and mechanically as required, in line with safe isolation procedures and permit-to-work requirements.

2.3 Re-pressurise the accessible pipework with oxygen-free nitrogen (OFN) to confirm/locate the exact position of Leaks 1, 2 and 3, and to investigate the possible fourth leak at the wall entry point as far as access allows.

2.4 Cut out and replace the three confirmed defective compression joints (Leaks 1–3) with new brazed joints, in line with good practice, to remove the risk of recurrence associated with compression fittings on this installation.

2.5 Investigate the possible fourth leak at the wall entry point. Where accessible, cut out and replace with a brazed joint. Where not accessible without opening up beyond the current work area, report findings and recommend next steps.

2.6 Check every remaining accessible compression joint on the roof-level pipework run (not just the identified leak points) using electronic leak detector and leak detection fluid, and replace any further compromised joints found with brazed joints.

2.7 Once all accessible joints are repaired/replaced, pressure test the full accessible circuit to the standard applied in the original test (40 bar strength test, 1 hour hold; 35 bar standing test) and confirm no further pressure loss.

2.8 Deep vacuum the system to remove air and moisture, and hold vacuum to confirm system integrity prior to re-gas.

2.9 Re-gas the system to the manufacturer's specified refrigerant charge weight.

2.10 Reinstate power and controls, and return the system to normal operation.

2.11 Function test the system on completion to confirm correct operation and cooling output.

2.12 Remove all tools, equipment and waste from site, leaving the work area clean and tidy.

2.13 Complete and issue F-Gas documentation, including refrigerant handling log, leak test certificate, and any waste transfer/consignment notes.

ACCESS TO FLOORS 1–6 (OUTSIDE DEMISE)

3.1 As every accessible joint tested was found to be compromised, there is a real risk that further joints on the same pipework run, between floors 6 and ground, are similarly affected. This cannot be confirmed or repaired under this scope, as floors 1–6 fall outside Neko Health's demise.

3.2 Should access to floors 1–6 be arranged with the landlord/managing agent, Up-fm will provide a revised scope and quotation to check and, where necessary, replace joints along the remainder of the pipe run.


EXCLUSIONS

4.1 Any works to pipework within floors 1–6, unless access is separately arranged and agreed. 4.2 Supply and cost of replacement refrigerant gas beyond standard system charge (unless quoted separately). 4.3 Repair or replacement of major components (compressors, coils, PCBs) unless found defective and agreed separately. 4.4 Making good of any builder's work/decoration disturbed to access pipework, unless specified. 4.5 Any warranty claim or recovery of costs from Oktra (original fit-out contractor) – this scope covers remedial works only.

HEALTH & SAFETY

5.1 All works to be carried out in accordance with a valid Risk Assessment and Method Statement (RAMS), submitted prior to works commencing. 5.2 Engineers to hold valid F-Gas qualification (Category 1) and relevant electrical/brazing competency. 5.3 Permit to work to be obtained from site management prior to isolation of any plant. 5.4 Appropriate PPE to be worn at all times, including roof access precautions.

PROGRAMME

6.1 Estimated duration on site: 5 days. 6.2 Client to confirm access arrangements no less than 48hrs prior to works.

REPORTING

7.1 A written report will be issued within  48 hours of completion of works, confirming joints repaired/replaced, final pressure test results, and system status. 7.2 Where access to floors 1–6 remains outstanding, the report will restate the residual risk and recommended next steps.

You are carrying out monthly sentinel temperature testing on the domestic hot and cold water systems.

- Test the first and last outlets on each hot and cold water line.
- Cold water should reach below 20°C within 2 minutes.
- Hot water should reach 50°C or above within 1 minute (55°C for healthcare sites).
- Record the temperature and the time taken to reach it.
- If temperatures are outside limits, recheck, report to the supervisor, and raise a note in Joblogic.

Sentinel Temperature Test (Tap Temperature Readings) - Monthly Visit

You are carrying out monthly sentinel temperature testing on the domestic hot and cold water systems.

The purpose of this task is to check that water temperatures are within safe limits to prevent the growth of Legionella bacteria.

- Test the first and last outlets on each hot and cold water line.
- Cold water should reach below 20C within 2 minutes.
- Hot water should reach 50C or above within 1 minute (55C for healthcare sites).
- Record the temperature and the time taken to reach it.
- If temperatures are outside limits, recheck, report to the supervisor, and raise a note in JobLogic.
- Wipe probes between each test and ensure readings are taken accurately.

Your aim is to confirm the system is performing correctly and identify any outlets or systems where temperatures suggest potential stagnation or risk of Legionella growth.

Flushing Infrequently Used Outlets - Weekly 

You are carrying out weekly flushing of low-usage water outlets to maintain water hygiene and prevent the growth of Legionella bacteria.
The purpose of this task is to ensure fresh water is drawn through outlets that are not used regularly (e.g. sinks, showers, or taps in quiet areas, meeting rooms, or spare offices).

What to do:
- Run cold and hot taps for a minimum of 2 minutes.
- Ensure water flows freely with no signs of stagnation, discolouration, or odour.
- Record each outlet flushed on the Joblogic form.
- Wipe taps and surrounding areas dry after flushing.

You are carrying out the monthly functional flick test on the building’s emergency lighting system to confirm all fittings operate correctly when the mains power is interrupted.

- Isolate the lighting circuit using the local key switch or test point for each area.
- Confirm that all emergency lights illuminate immediately when power is cut.

- Damaged or failed lamps/LEDs
- Cracked or missing diffusers
- Incorrect or missing labelling
After checks, restore mains power and confirm charging indicators (usually green LEDs) are lit.
